A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same NEPENTHE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification experiments, pruning trajectories, layer-removal results, and component and activation ablations in Section 4 and the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains original vision experiments and adds NLP evaluations, pruning variants, efficiency measurements, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The core entropy-guided iterative pruning framework remains. However, Equation (13) changes from averaging neuron-level entropy–magnitude products to multiplying layer-average entropy by layer-average magnitude, which is generally non-equivalent. v2 also introduces variants incorporating SSL regularization and replacing magnitude pruning with Wanda. These are revisions and extensions within the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 extends the vision-only evaluation to SST-2 sentiment classification, QNLI and RTE language-inference tasks, and the MMLU high-school US-history subset. The original vision datasets remain; ImageNet was already evaluated in v1's supplement.

E2.justification: v2 removes the evaluated Layer Folding comparisons from v1 Tables 2 and 21. It retains IMP and adds smallest-weight and smallest-gradient layer removal, HRank on CIFAR-10, group lasso, and EGP comparisons. Table 5 also adds a depth-matched model trained from initialization.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce ResNet-50/152 and MobileNetV2-0.75 configurations, three-epoch AdamW NLP training, FP16 Llama evaluation without fine-tuning, a depth-matched initialization control, and sharpness and hardware-efficiency measurements. The shared vision training schedules and augmentation policies remain unchanged between v1 Table 5 and v2 Appendix C.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and activation studies, v2 adds pruning-rate sensitivity, a Swin-T/Tiny-ImageNet component ablation, the initialization control, loss-landscape sharpness analysis, SSL and Wanda variants, and comparative layer-removal diagnostics. Appendix D.5 adds weight and activation histograms to examine the Gaussian assumptions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or performance uncertainty bars. v2's new histograms describe weight and activation distributions rather than uncertainty in experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: The detailed original vision trajectories and ImageNet scores are retained, but v2 adds NLP/LLM, model-scaling, sharpness, pruning-variant, and efficiency results and removes Layer Folding results. For example, Table 10 newly reports 3.32 ms dense versus 2.96 ms pruned inference time for ResNet-18/CIFAR-10. Some IMP summary scores differ from retained appendix values without clarified iteration selection, preventing direct performance-change conclusions.

T1.justification: v2 adds smooth-rectifier approximation and propagated-error bounds in Appendix A and a formal ReLU6 interval analysis in Appendix B. It also corrects the state definition to use pre-activations and changes Equation (11)'s probability event from Z > 0 to Z > epsilon. These extend and revise the earlier mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The entropy-guided depth-reduction claim remains, but v2 broadens the claimed applicability to NLP and pruning criteria beyond magnitude. Its conclusion additionally presents unstructured pruning as implicit depth regularization producing flatter loss landscapes. The earlier claim of being the first unstructured method to reduce network depth is dropped.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of baseline failures, flatness and generalization, and latency savings despite possible sparsity fill-in. It explicitly qualifies smooth-rectifier linearization and identifies average neuron entropy as a proxy rather than joint entropy. Conversely, v1's explicit discussion of failure on underfitting ImageNet models disappears, although the corresponding results remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds NLP optimizer settings, sequence length, prunable-layer details, GPU identification, hardware-specific measurements, and training-time columns in the detailed result tables. Its abstract supplies a code-repository URL where v1 promised future release, although Appendix C retains the older release wording.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially through discussion of Wanda, HRank, SSL, EASIER, and transformer layer merging. The already cited Liao et al. (2023) work is now explicitly identified as EGP, evaluated, and positioned as the closest predecessor. This materially revises the novelty positioning rather than merely expanding references.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, experimental narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around layer collapse. The method subsections are consolidated, the experiments are reorganized, and the supplement is restructured into thematic Appendices A–D.

P2.justification: Table 2 is reorganized with model groups and dataset columns, and detailed tables gain training-time columns. The pseudocode is split into two algorithms, Figure 1 is revised, and Figure 3 is resized and relabeled. New comparison curves, interval diagrams, hardware tables, and distribution panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central generality and efficiency claims through NLP evaluations, a depth-matched control, sensitivity analyses, and measured deployment benefits that v1 did not provide. The approximation and entropy-proxy qualifications also improve interpretability. These gains outweigh the removed Layer Folding comparisons and explicit ImageNet failure discussion, although insufficiently reconciled summary and appendix scores remain a material reporting weakness.
